title: The Cadaver Synod — a Pope dug up his dead predecessor for trial
hook: THE POPE PUT A CORPSE ON TRIAL
voiceover: In the year 897, Pope Stephen VI had his predecessor, Pope Formosus, dug up out of the ground. Eight months after his death. Then Stephen put the corpse on trial. They dressed the body in papal robes. Sat him in a chair. A young deacon spoke for him. The dead pope was found guilty. They cut off three fingers from his right hand — the ones he used to give blessings — and threw his body in the Tiber River. The whole thing is called the Cadaver Synod. And yes, all of this is real history. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
emphasis: threw his body in the river
